version: Compose Multiplatform 1.12.2 (Jetpack Compose 1.12.1 base); Kotlin 2.4.21; Skiko 0.150.2; kotlinx-coroutines 1.11.0; JVM OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM 25.0.4.1+1-1-24.04.4-Ubuntu; GC G1 Young Generation+G1 Concurrent GC+G1 Old Generation

gc.source: GarbageCollectorMXBean count/time deltas between markers; max = max GcInfo.duration from GC notifications (ms resolution)

notes: frame_ms = interval between consecutive post-present timestamps: in each withFrameNanos callback (Compose FrameRecomposer.performFrame, which runs at the START of the frame, before measure/layout/draw) the app posts java.awt.EventQueue.invokeLater; Skiko's FrameDispatcher runs update+draw+finishFrame (SOFTWARE_FAST: raster surface -> X11 put image) inside the same EDT event, so the posted runnable runs right after finishFrame returned = the latest public post-render signal. Redraw is continuous (each frame requests the next one and changes content). Pacing (ops.pacing): '60' (default) = Skiko's native limiter kept on (public property skiko.vsync.enabled=true, Skiko default: software redrawer awaits FrameLimiter = 1000/displayRefreshRate) BUT under Xvfb it does not cap (measured ~170 fps on list: the refresh rate Skiko reads natively from X11 is not 60), so the app paces with a public API: at the start of every frame (withFrameNanos callback, EDT, runs before measure/layout/draw of that frame, including frames driven by Compose animations) it parks (LockSupport.parkNanos) until an absolute deadline grid of 16.667 ms, re-anchored after a missed deadline; 'uncapped' = skiko.vsync.enabled=false and no app pacing. images: LazyVerticalGrid 9 cols x 128dp (key=index, one contentType); each PNG decoded (Skia) and downscaled to 128x128 on demand when its item is first composed (warm-up included, same script), once, on 2 background threads (Dispatchers.Default.limitedParallelism(2)), placeholder until ready; bitmaps set immutable (avoids a pixel copy per draw in SkiaBackedCanvas.drawImageRect -> Image.makeFromBitmap); Image() default FilterQuality.Low (bilinear, no mipmaps); zoom 1->3->1 / 6 s + pan via one graphicsLayer (state read in the layer block: no recomposition). images_decoded / decode_total_ms (sum of per-image decode times) cover the whole run incl. warm-up.
